2027-05-25.title: Tuesday of the Eighth Week in Ordinary Time · St Bede the Venerable; St Gregory VII; St Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi
readings: Give to the Most High as he has given to you, and as generously as you can afford
To the upright I will show the saving power of God
who will not receive a hundredfold now in this age … with persecutions … and in the age to come eternal life
2027-05-25.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 8 (Year I). Three optional memorials may be kept today: St Bede the Venerable, priest and doctor of the Church; St Gregory VII, pope; St Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi, virgin. The first reading is given in NRSV numbering (Lectionary Sirach 35:1–12 = NRSV 35:1–15). Liturgical colour: green (white if a memorial is kept).
2027-05-25.verse: With every gift show a cheerful face, and dedicate your tithe with gladness. Give to the Most High as he has given to you, and as generously as you can afford.
theo: Ben Sira, the wise teacher of Jerusalem, wrote about two centuries before Christ, when the Temple sacrifices were offered every day. He loved the Temple, and he does not mock the sacrifices. But he wants his students to understand what makes an offering pleasing to God. He begins with a surprising list: “The one who keeps the law makes many offerings; one who heeds the commandments makes an offering of well-being. The one who returns a kindness offers choice flour, and one who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering.” Kindness repaid, alms given, a commandment kept: each of these is already an offering laid on God's altar. “To keep from wickedness is pleasing to the Lord, and to forsake unrighteousness is an atonement.” Then he turns to the gifts themselves, and his advice is warm and practical: “Do not appear before the Lord empty-handed.” “Be generous when you worship the Lord, and do not stint the first fruits of your hands. With every gift show a cheerful face, and dedicate your tithe with gladness.” The measure is simple: “Give to the Most High as he has given to you, and as generously as you can afford. For the Lord is the one who repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.” And one warning: “Do not offer him a bribe, for he will not accept it.” God cannot be bought. The Psalm says the same thing in God's own voice: “Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you,” but “offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving,” for “those who bring thanksgiving as their sacrifice honor me.”

In the Gospel Peter speaks for all the Twelve. They have just watched a rich young man walk away sad, and heard Jesus say how hard it is for the wealthy to enter the kingdom. Peter blurts out: “Look, we have left everything and followed you.” There is a question hidden in the sentence: and what will we get? Jesus does not scold him. He answers with a promise that is both generous and honest: “there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields, for my sake and for the sake of the good news, who will not receive a hundredfold now in this age.” The hundredfold is real: the one who leaves a family for Christ finds brothers and sisters and mothers in every Christian community, houses opened in every town. But Jesus adds two words no salesman would add: “with persecutions.” And then the true reward: “in the age to come eternal life.” Ben Sira said God repays sevenfold; Jesus says a hundredfold. You cannot outgive God. St Bede the Venerable, whom the Church remembers today, gave his whole life from the age of seven to the monastery of Jarrow in northern England. He never travelled far, yet through his books he taught all of Europe. Tradition says that on his last day he finished dictating a passage of St John's Gospel in English and died singing “Glory be to the Father.” That is the cheerful face Ben Sira asks for, kept to the end.
outline: Ask: when you put money in the collection, or give your time, what does your face look like?
Point 1 · Every good deed is an offering
Kindness repaid and alms given are sacrifices pleasing to God.
Give as God has given you, gladly, without trying to bribe him.
Jesus' honest promise to those who leave all for him.
“Give to the Most High as he has given to you.”
live: Choose one gift today, money, time or help, and give it with a smile, without telling anyone.
Tonight name three people God has given you as brothers and sisters in faith, and thank him for each.
2027-05-25.prayer: Most High God, everything we have has come from your hand. Teach us to give back to you as you have given to us, generously and with a cheerful face, not to buy your favour but to thank you for it. Lord Jesus, you promised a hundredfold to all who leave everything for your sake; give us courage when following you costs us something, and keep our eyes on the life of the age to come. Through the prayers of St Bede the Venerable, may we serve you gladly to our last breath. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the priest says: blessed are you, Lord God of all creation, for through your goodness we have received the bread and wine we offer you. We bring back to God what he first gave us, and he returns it a hundredfold: the bread becomes the Body of Christ, the wine his Blood, and our small offering is united to the one perfect sacrifice of his Son.

quick: Ben Sira teaches that keeping the commandments, repaying kindness and giving alms are offerings pleasing to God.
Give to God as he has given to you, generously and with a cheerful face; God cannot be bribed, but he repays sevenfold.
Jesus promises those who leave everything for him a hundredfold now, with persecutions, and eternal life in the age to come.
2027-05-25.action: Give one gift today, of money, time or help, quietly and with a smile.
2027-05-25.question: When I give to God or to others, do I give gladly, or with a long face?
kidsaint: When Bede was only seven years old, his family took him to a monastery in England, and he lived there all his life. He loved to study, to pray and to sing. He wrote many books about the Bible and about the history of the Church in England, so people call him the father of English history. On the last day of his life he was still helping a young monk to write, and he died singing Glory be to the Father. Lesson: use the gifts God gives you to help others learn about him, every day of your life.

family.explain: Ben Sira was a wise teacher long ago. He said: when you give something to God, give it with a happy face! God gave us everything, our home, our food, our family, so we should give back gladly. Jesus told Peter that anyone who gives up something for him will get back a hundred times more, a big family of brothers and sisters in the Church.
family.intention: We pray for the poor who will receive our alms, and for people who are treated badly because they follow Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing our family can give this week, with a smile?”

illus: A parish priest in Alappuzha used to watch the collection basket go round at Sunday Mass. He noticed that a fisherwoman who sold fish at the market every morning always dropped in her coin with a little smile and a sign of the cross. One day he asked her why. She said: Father, God gave me the sea and the fish and the strength to carry the basket; this is only a little of his own money that I am giving back to him. The priest said later that her coin taught him more about Sirach 35 than any commentary. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, everything we have is yours. Teach us to give back to you gladly, and keep us faithful to Jesus whatever it costs. Amen.
share: One who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering (Sirach 35:4). Which of my ordinary good deeds could I offer to God as a sacrifice today?
With every gift show a cheerful face (Sirach 35:11). Is there something I give, at home or in the parish, with a grumbling heart?
Look, we have left everything and followed you (Mark 10:28). What has following Jesus cost me, and what have I received in return?
pm.resp: To the upright I will show the saving power of God.
interc: For the Church, that her members may give generously and gladly to the poor and to the work of the Gospel.
For Christians who suffer persecution for the name of Jesus, especially in India and across Asia.
For priests and religious who have left home and family for Christ, that they may find the hundredfold he promised.
For teachers and scholars, through the prayers of St Bede, that they may serve the truth.
For our group, that we may never try to bargain with God, but trust his generosity.
pm.close: Father, you are never outdone in generosity. Accept the offering of our lives, and give us joy in serving you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the wise man Ben Sira lived at a time when the Temple in Jerusalem was full of sacrifices: lambs, bulls, flour, oil. He loved the Temple. But he tells us that there are other sacrifices too. The one who returns a kindness offers choice flour, and one who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering (Sirach 35:3–4). A kind word to a neighbour, a coin to a beggar, a commandment kept when it is hard: all of these are laid on God's altar.

Then he says something very human: with every gift show a cheerful face (Sirach 35:11). We all know people who give, but with a long face, so that everyone knows how much it cost them. Ben Sira says: do not give like that. Give to the Most High as he has given to you. God did not give us life and family and daily bread with a long face. He gave gladly. Our giving should look like his.

And he warns us: do not offer him a bribe, for he will not accept it (Sirach 35:14). Sometimes we treat God like an officer who must be pleased before he signs our paper. I will give this candle, this offering, if you give me that job. God is not like that. We give because he has already given, not to buy his favour.

In the Gospel Peter asks the question we all ask quietly: Look, we have left everything and followed you. What will we get? Jesus answers: a hundredfold now in this age, with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life (Mark 10:30). He does not hide the cost. But he promises that nobody who gives to him will be the loser. Today, let us give something gladly, and trust the God who repays sevenfold and a hundredfold. Amen.
kids: Children, imagine your friend gives you a present but makes a grumpy face while giving it. Would you be happy? A wise man in the Bible says: when you give something to God, give it with a smiling face! Jesus told his friends: if you give up something for me, I will give you back a hundred times more. God is the most generous Giver of all. Let us give to him with a big smile!

intro: Theme: “Give to the Most High as he has given to you.”
Every good deed an offering, every gift given gladly, and a God who repays a hundredfold.

points.h: Every good deed is an offering
q: The one who returns a kindness offers choice flour, and one who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering.
Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.
points.apply: Tonight, before sleeping, offer to God the good things you did today, however small, as your evening sacrifice.

sub: As generously as you can afford.
q: Those who bring thanksgiving as their sacrifice honor me; to those who go the right way I will show the salvation of God.
Each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
points.apply: Decide this week what you will give to the poor or to the parish, and give it gladly, without complaint or display.

sub: Eternal life in the age to come.
q: For the Lord is the one who repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.
But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.
points.apply: Thank God this week for one person in the Church who has been a brother, sister, father or mother to you, and tell that person so.

concl: Ben Sira teaches that the best offering is a life of kindness and alms, given with a cheerful face.
Jesus promises that no one who gives to him will lose: a hundredfold now, with persecutions, and eternal life to come.
2027-05-25.resolve: Give one gift each day this week, gladly and quietly, as an offering to God.
